topics: Root cause analysis: control-plane network partition + autoscaler bug
Immediate mitigations and long-term reliability improvements
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sophie Martins (Argosy CTO), Rajiv Patel (Argosy SRE Lead), Elena Lopez (Argosy Director of Product)

Summary: quick postmortem follow-up to walk through RCA artifacts, confirm mitigations and owners, schedule testing.

[00:00] Maya: hi everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the postmortem artifacts we sent and make sure next steps are clear. grade: apologies for the noisy one earlier, um--
[00:18] Sophie: no worries, we appreciate you pulling this together. we've read the draft and had questions on the autoscaler interaction with the dedicated pool.
[00:30] Liam: sure, quick context — during the window on 6/15 we saw an intermittent network partition between the control plane and the dedicated GPU pool in us-east. that caused health checks to flap, which then triggered the autoscaler to evict nodes and re-provision; there was also an edge case where the scale down logic didn't account for in-flight KV cache warms, so several requests hit partially-loaded model shards and fell back to a slower hosted model which increased latency and error rates.
[01:05] Rajiv: just to be clear, when you say control plane partition, was that an AWS networking issue or something internal to redwood?
[01:12] Liam: initial traces showed TCP resets on the control-plane-side BGP peer — it looks like a short-lived route instability in our colo provider, but the autoscaler logic's timing amplified the impact. our logs show the timeline.
[01:30] Maya: we uploaded the raw logs and a condensed timeline to the shared folder (link: https://redwood.example.com/argosy/incidents/2027-06-15). please tell us if anything is missing.
[01:48] Elena: saw that, thanks. the part that worries our team is the failover behavior — some of our endpoints experienced timeouts for a couple of minutes which cascaded into our user-facing queues.
[02:05] Liam: yeah that's a big flag; our immediate mitigation is a config change to the autoscaler to increase healthcheck grace period from 10s to 45s and to stop killing nodes with non-empty KV caches. we've got a patch ready, just need sign-off and a deployment window.
[02:30] Sophie: ok, what about the fallback to hosted model — that was helpful to keep service up, but it spiked cost. we need a predictable fallback policy and a rate-limited fan-out.
[02:45] Maya: agreed; proposing a policy: first try dedicated pool, if latency > 1.5s for 30s route to reserved hosted pool with a token cap, then circuit-break for 2m. we can make that configurable per-route.
[03:10] Rajiv: can that be done without changing our client-side retries? our app does aggressive retries which amplified load.
[03:20] Liam: yes we'll add server-side circuit-break and rate-limit before doing client-visible errors; client retries should be adjusted too, but we can mitigate server-side.
[03:35] Elena: what's the plan for verifying the autoscaler patch? we don't want regressions during peak.
[03:42] Liam: staging test first: run synthetic traffic at peak QPS plus injection of network partition simulated by dropping control-plane heartbeats. we will validate no node evictions and that KV cache warm is preserved.
[04:00] Maya: we've proposed the staging window for 6/25 and a rollout to prod with canary traffic on 6/27.
[04:12] Sophie: that timeline works for us if we get the detailed steps and rollback plan.

[04:30] -- Transcript excerpts / Q&A --
[04:30] Rajiv: one more technical question — the logs show "kv-cache load incomplete" message, is that a redwood runtime message or from the model server?
[04:40] Liam: runtime message; the runtime retries the kv-cache populate but doesn't block the request path leading to partial responses. we'll update to block and return controlled 503s until warmed or route to hosted fallback.
[05:00] Sophie: will blocking cause user-visible errors? we need to balance between degraded responses and errors.
[05:06] Liam: yes it's tradeoff; we'll expose a setting: soft-block (serve partial with warning header) or hard-block (503). recommend soft-block in canary then evaluate.

[06:15] Maya: shifting to runbook: we've sketched a new playbook in the doc, adding steps to verify network health, to check BGP peers, to delay autoscaler action, and to force a graceful eviction route. link: (doc link).
[06:38] Elena: who on redwood will own the runbook updates?
[06:42] Maya: Liam will author the detailed runbook updates, I'll coordinate approval and the share.

[07:00] Rajiv: what monitoring changes are you proposing?
[07:06] Liam: add an alert for control-plane heartbeats mismatch, alert for kv-cache warm percentage < 90% for >30s, and an incident dashboard with token-level latency. we'll also add a synthetic probe that exercises dedicated pool every minute.
[07:30] Sophie: can you send the exact alert thresholds? we want to map to our pager schedule.
[07:36] Maya: yes, we'll include alert thresholds in the follow-up email.

[08:00] Elena: cost impact from fallback to hosted — do you have an estimate for the 6/15 window?
[08:08] Liam: preliminary estimate shows hosted fallback added ~ $6k of incremental cost during the 18-minute tail. full cost calc in doc.
[08:18] Sophie: ok we'll review; we're more concerned about reliability but cost is important.

[09:00] Maya: quick recap of mitigations: (1) autoscaler patch (longer grace, don't evict non-empty cache), (2) route-level fallback policy and server-side circuit-break, (3) runbook and alerts, (4) synthetic testing and staging validation.
[09:25] Rajiv: sounds good. two asks from our side: ensure the patch is backported to our pinned runtime branch, and provide a hotfix path for the next 48h if anything regresses.
[09:38] Liam: backport is in the plan; hotfix channel will be on standby, Liam + Maya will be on-call for the rollout window.

[10:00] -- Action / scheduling --
[10:00] Maya: proposed schedule: 6/23 final postmortem and logs; 6/25 staging test (09:00-11:00 UTC); 6/27 canary rollout (low traffic window) with rollback plan; 6/30 runbook review and DR drill.
[10:20] Sophie: confirmed, we'll block time and align internal stakeholders.
[10:30] Elena: please also include the list of SSO/IDP tokens we used for the runbook to avoid access delays.
[10:40] Maya: noted, will include.

[11:00] -- Closing remarks --
[11:00] Sophie: appreciate the thoroughness. main concern for us is minimizing user impact and predictable failover; the plan addresses this.
[11:12] Maya: thanks all, we'll share the updated postmortem doc and assign action items; talk soon.
[11:20] Liam: logging one minor note — there are some transcription typos in the raw trace ("KV cash" etc) we'll annotate the artifacts.
[11:28] End meeting.
